binders: fp is an arbitrary augmented real addition model. Write u for its real unit-roundoff parameter, flAdd for its modeled binary addition, and twoSum for its paired high-and-residual operation.
n is an arbitrary natural number, including zero.
v is an arbitrary function Fin(n+1) -> Real, equivalently an arbitrary real vector (v_0,...,v_n) of exactly n+1 components.
hvalid is a proof of the strict validity condition (n+1)u < 1, where n+1 is cast to a real.
hypotheses: For every real x, flAdd(0,x) = x.
For every ordered pair of reals x,y, there exists a real delta depending on x and y such that |delta| <= u and flAdd(x,y) = (x+y)(1+delta).
For every pair a,b, if twoSum(a,b) = (h,l), then h = flAdd(a,b).
For every pair a,b, if twoSum(a,b) = (h,l), then h+l = a+b exactly.
For every pair a,b, if twoSum(a,b) = (h,l), then |l| <= u|h|.
conclusions: If C is the level-2 computed sum defined below, S = sum from i=0 to n of v_i, A = sum from i=0 to n of |v_i|, and gamma_n(u) = nu/(1-nu), then |C-S| <= u|S| + gamma_n(u)^2 A.
mathematical_definitions: Define the exact sum S = sum_{i=0}^n v_i and A = sum_{i=0}^n |v_i|. The latter is the finite l1 norm of v.
Define gamma_n(u) = ((n as a real)u)/(1-(n as a real)u).
Define p_0 = v_0. For j = 0,...,n-1, define (p_{j+1},e_{j+1}) = twoSum(p_j,v_{j+1}). Thus p_{j+1} = flAdd(p_j,v_{j+1}), p_{j+1}+e_{j+1} = p_j+v_{j+1}, and |e_{j+1}| <= u|p_{j+1}|.
Define the once-transformed vector w of length n+1 by w_j = e_{j+1} for 0 <= j < n and w_n = p_n. When n=0, this simply means w_0 = p_0 = v_0.
Define Seq_fl([]) = 0, Seq_fl([x_0]) = x_0, and for a list of at least two entries define Seq_fl([x_0,...,x_m]) = flAdd(Seq_fl([x_0,...,x_{m-1}]),x_m).
The computed quantity is C = Seq_fl([w_0,...,w_n]). This is LocalDef006(fp,v): level K=2 performs K-1=1 transformation and then one left-to-right modeled summation.
The exact-decomposition equations imply that the exact real sum of the transformed vector w is S.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonempty real vector v=(v_0,...,v_n) and every augmented addition model satisfying the stated relative-error and exact-residual axioms, if (n+1)u<1, perform one twoSum-based transformation: accumulate high partial sums p_j, store each exact residual e_j, place the final high sum last, and then sum that transformed vector from left to right with flAdd. The resulting value C differs from the exact sum S by at most u times |S| plus the square of nu/(1-nu) times the componentwise absolute-value sum of v.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The vector always has length n+1, so empty input vectors are not covered. The case n=0 is included and represents a singleton vector.
The conclusion is conditional on a supplied proof of (n+1)u<1. When this inequality is false, the declaration makes no claim; viewed as an implication, it is vacuous.
Because u>=0 is built into fp and (n+1)u<1, one has nu<1, so the denominator 1-nu in gamma_n(u) is strictly positive and nonzero.
The gamma factor uses n, while the validity condition uses n+1; these are distinct quantities exactly as encoded.
Level K=2 means one transformation, not two transformations, because the algorithm iterates the transformation K-1 times using truncated natural subtraction.
The computation order is fixed: high partial sums process v_1 through v_n in increasing index order, and the transformed vector is then summed left-to-right.
No sign, magnitude, nonzero, ordering, representability, or conditioning assumptions are imposed on the entries v_i; they are arbitrary real numbers.

All arithmetic is modeled by functions on exact real numbers. The proposition does not encode a finite representable set, overflow, underflow, subnormal behavior, infinities, NaNs, or a concrete machine implementation.
The twoSum operation is assumed axiomatically to return an exactly decomposing residual satisfying |l|<=u|h|. The proposition does not prove that a particular implementation has these properties.
The result is an absolute forward-error bound. It does not assert a relative-error ratio when S is nonzero, and when S=0 the u|S| term vanishes but the gamma_n(u)^2 A term can remain.
The componentwise sum A is the l1 norm; no Euclidean, maximum, or operator norm occurs.
No claim is made for other compensation levels, alternative summation orders, or vectors of a different dimension under the same n.
